mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions and accelerating economic growth, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, it signals a tightening labor market and accelerating economic expansion, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in stronger corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 5.0), or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong aggregate demand and economic momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved consumer spending and corporate revenue outlooks.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * HOUST) fails to produce a positive Rank IC above 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the Federal Reserve's policy stance compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or the average return in tightening periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and supply chain strength, which typically supports corporate profitability and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2000, it signals a weakening housing market and reduced consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST < 2000), or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint effect of rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and falling federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a stagflationary environment where inflation erodes real returns and monetary policy fails to support growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (CPIAUCSL * FEDFUNDS) fails to produce a negative Rank IC below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (UNRATE < 4.5 and INDPRO > 110), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and reduced growth momentum, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in economic slowdown risks.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods meeting the late-cycle condition (UNRATE < 4.5 AND INDPRO > 110), or the average return in late-cycle periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
